title: CORNER Go-To-Market Playbook
summary: How AOM gets the first 15 paying Corner clients. Sales channels, conversion funnel, objection handling, pricing presentation, and the 90-day launch sprint. Built for Patrik + Ash + Jacob.
content:
CORNER Go-To-Market Playbook

Author: Steve (AI Advisory Lead) Date: 2026-03-16 For: Patrik (closes deals), Ash (operations), Jacob (outreach), Alex (positioning) Goal: 15 paying Corner clients within 6 months of C4 launch

The Starting Position

AOM has everything except clients:

  • A working product (AOM runs on it daily)
  • A website with funnel pages (/system, /roi-calculator, /book, /audit/test)
  • 51+ outreach emails sent, 33 drafts pending
  • CPA phone scripts ready
  • AZ ROC contractor database (45k+ records, pending download)
  • An audit questionnaire (27 questions, 6 sections)
  • Pricing model ($1,500-$10,000/month)
  • A case study (AOM itself)

What's missing: a repeatable sales playbook. This document is that playbook.

Target Client Profile

Ideal first client:

  • Industry: Construction (HVAC, plumbing, electrical, general contractor) or CPA firm
  • Size: 5-25 employees
  • Revenue: $500k-$5M/year
  • Location: Phoenix metro
  • Pain: overwhelmed by admin, missing leads, bad at follow-up, working 60+ hours/week
  • Attitude: curious about AI but doesn't know where to start
  • Budget: can absorb $3k/month if they see the value (it's less than one employee)

Disqualified clients (don't waste time):

  • Under $300k/year revenue (can't afford it, will churn)
  • Over $50M revenue (need enterprise sales cycle we can't support yet)
  • Not in Phoenix metro (can't visit, can't build the relationship, can't do on-site demos)
  • Anti-technology (will resist adoption, will blame the tool for their unwillingness to change)
  • Already have a CTO or IT director (they'll try to build it themselves, or they'll be territorial)

Sales Channels (Ranked by Expected ROI)

Channel 1: Warm Network (Highest Conversion)

Who: People Patrik and Ash already know. Ambition Mechanical referrals. Past clients. Chamber of Commerce contacts. Industry contacts.

Why first: Trust is pre-built. Conversion rate on warm leads in B2B SaaS is 5-15x higher than cold outreach. The first 3-5 clients will almost certainly come from here.

Play:

  1. Patrik and Ash each list 20 business owners they know personally
  2. Send a personal message (not an email blast): "We built something for ourselves and it's working. Would love to show you. 15 minutes."
  3. In-person demo preferred (coffee shop, their office, or AOM's space)
  4. Demo on Patrik's actual Corner instance. Show real agents doing real work. Not a slide deck.
  5. Close with: "We're taking 5 businesses for the first cohort. $3k/month. We build everything for you."

Target: 5 clients from warm network within 90 days of C4 launch.

Channel 2: Cold Outreach (Highest Volume)

Who: Phoenix-area contractors and CPA firms. From AZ ROC database and public CPA directories.

Why: Volume. 15,000+ licensed contractors in Phoenix alone. Even at 0.5% conversion, that's 75 clients.

Play:

  1. Jacob segments AZ ROC database: HVAC, plumbing, electrical, GC. Filter: active license, Phoenix metro, estimated 5-25 employees.
  2. 3-email sequence per prospect (see Email Sequences below)
  3. Email 1: open the door. Email 2: value-add (market breakdown doc). Email 3: direct CTA.
  4. Responses route to Patrik for scheduling
  5. 15-minute discovery call (see Discovery Call Script below)
  6. In-person demo for qualified prospects

Target: 5 clients from cold outreach within 6 months.

Channel 3: Content + Inbound (Slowest but Compounds)

Who: Business owners searching for AI solutions, reading about AI for small business, seeing AOM's content on LinkedIn/social.

Why: Compounds over time. A blog post about "AI for HVAC companies" generates leads for years.

Play:

  1. Alex drafts 2 LinkedIn posts/week from Patrik's account
  2. Blog posts on aheadofmarket.com targeting search terms: "AI for construction companies", "AI for CPAs", "AI operations for small business"
  3. Case study on AOM's own transformation (video + written)
  4. /system page on aheadofmarket.com continues to drive bookings
  5. /roi-calculator proves the value before anyone talks to Patrik

Target: 3 clients from inbound within 6 months.

Channel 4: Referral Program (Force Multiplier)

Who: Existing clients referring other business owners.

Why: Referred clients close 4x faster and churn 37% less than non-referred clients (Wharton School study).

Play:

  1. After 30 days of successful Corner usage, ask: "Who do you know that's drowning in admin?"
  2. Incentive: $500 credit on their next month for every referral that signs up
  3. Make it easy: Patrik sends the referral a personal message, not a form

Target: 2 clients from referrals within 6 months (after first few clients are established).

The Funnel

AWARENESS -> INTEREST -> DEMO -> TRIAL -> CLOSE -> EXPAND

Stage 1: Awareness

  • How they find out: cold email, LinkedIn post, warm intro, search, word of mouth
  • Goal: they know Corner exists and know what it does (one sentence)

Stage 2: Interest

  • How they engage: visit aheadofmarket.com/system, use the ROI calculator, read a blog post, reply to an email
  • Goal: they think "this might work for me"

Stage 3: Demo

  • How it happens: 15-minute discovery call, then in-person demo on Patrik's live instance
  • Goal: they see their business reflected in the product. "This is what my operations could look like."

Stage 4: Trial

  • How it happens: 7-day free trial (when self-service launches in C5). Before C5: AOM builds their instance during a 2-week audit engagement ($2,500).
  • Goal: they use it daily for a week and can't imagine going back

Stage 5: Close

  • How it happens: Patrik walks them through pricing. $3k/month Growth tier. Compare to the cost of one employee ($4-6k/month fully loaded). ROI calculator proves the math.
  • Goal: signed. Card on file. First month charged.

Stage 6: Expand

  • After 3-6 months: add more agents, upgrade tier, add team members (C7)
  • After 12 months: the referral engine kicks in. This client generates 1-2 more clients per year.

Pre-C4 Sales Motion (The Audit Bridge)

C4 isn't shipped yet. Containers don't exist. But AOM can sell the audit TODAY.

The audit ($2,500) is the foot in the door:

  1. Patrik conducts the audit using the 27-question questionnaire
  2. 2-week engagement: understand the business, map their operations, identify AI opportunities
  3. Deliverable: written report with specific recommendations and projected ROI
  4. The report naturally leads to: "We can build this for you. $3k/month."
  5. If they say yes, they're first in line when C4 launches

Why this works:

  • Revenue today (not waiting for C4)
  • Validates the sales process
  • Builds case studies
  • Creates urgency: "We're onboarding our first cohort now"
  • The audit IS the onboarding process. By the time it's done, AOM already knows enough about the business to configure their Corner instance

Target: 3-5 audits before C4 launches.

Discovery Call Script (15 Minutes)

Goal: Qualify the prospect and book a demo.

Minute 0-2: Warm-up "Thanks for taking the time. Quick background: we're a small team in Phoenix building AI operations systems for [their industry]. We built one for ourselves first and it's running our entire back office. Now we're bringing it to other businesses. I want to learn about your operations and see if this is a fit."

Minute 2-7: Discovery questions (pick 3-4)

  • "Walk me through a typical day. What eats the most time?"
  • "How do you handle scheduling / estimating / client follow-up right now?"
  • "What falls through the cracks? What gets missed?"
  • "How many hours a week do you spend on admin vs. the actual work?"
  • "Have you tried any tools to help? What worked, what didn't?"
  • "If you could hire one person to handle the back office, what would they do?"

Minute 7-10: Position Corner "So what you're describing is exactly what we built this for. Corner gives you a team of AI agents that handles [their specific pain points from discovery]. Not a chatbot. A team. One handles your scheduling. One handles client communication. One tracks your pipeline. They work together, like real employees."

Minute 10-12: The proof "We're not theoretical. We run our own business on this system. 14 agents. Every day. I can show you what that looks like in a 20-minute demo. You'll see your industry, your tasks, your operations. No slides. Live system."

Minute 12-15: Close for demo "I'd love to show you this in person. Can I come by your office this week? Or I can demo it over a call if that's easier. Takes about 20 minutes."

If they're not ready for a demo: "Totally fair. Let me send you our market breakdown for [their industry]. Shows what other [contractors/CPAs] are doing with AI right now. Quick read. If it resonates, we'll talk."

Demo Script (20 Minutes, In-Person or Screen Share)

Goal: Show the live product. Close for audit or trial.

Setup: Patrik opens his actual Corner instance on his laptop. The demo is real. Not a prototype.

Minute 0-3: Context "This is my actual office. These are my real agents. They've been running my operations for months. Let me show you what they do."

Minute 3-8: Walk the office

  • Show the isometric view. Agents moving, working.
  • Click Bobby: "This is my web developer. He's built our entire website. 100+ commits."
  • Click Operations: "This is my chief of staff. She routes work, tracks priorities, closes loops."
  • Click Calendar: "This manages both my personal and work calendars."
  • Switch to Checklist mode: "This is the simple view. Everything my agents are working on."
  • Switch to Megaboard: "This is the stats view. Hours saved, tasks completed, ROI."

Minute 8-13: Mirror to their business "Now imagine this for [their business]. Instead of Bobby building websites, your Bobby handles [their specific task]. Instead of my Calendar agent, yours manages [their scheduling complexity]. Instead of my Outreach agent, yours follows up with [their leads/clients]."

Tailor the agent names and descriptions to their industry. For a plumber: "Your Estimating agent handles quotes. Your Dispatch agent manages the crew schedule. Your Client Comms agent follows up after every job."

Minute 13-17: The math "Let me show you the numbers." Open the ROI calculator.

  • Input their approximate hours spent on admin per week
  • Show the dollar value of time saved
  • Compare: "Corner is $3k/month. That's less than one part-time employee. And it works 24/7."

Minute 17-20: Close "We're taking our first cohort of businesses right now. Here's what getting started looks like: we do a 2-week audit of your operations. $2,500 flat. We learn your business inside and out and show you exactly where AI saves you the most time. If you love what you see, we build your Corner office and you're running by month 2."

If they ask for a free trial: "The audit IS the trial. We spend two weeks inside your business. If at the end of two weeks you don't see the value, you've got a written report of your operational bottlenecks that's useful regardless. No risk."

Email Sequences

Sequence 1: Construction Companies (Cold)

Email 1: Open the door (Day 0)

Subject: Quick question about [Company Name]

Hi [First Name],

I run a production and AI company here in Phoenix. We've been working with local contractors, and I had a question:

How are you handling scheduling and client follow-up right now?

We built an AI system that runs the back office for businesses like yours. Not a chatbot. A full operations team that works 24/7. One of our contractor clients saved 15+ hours a week in admin time.

If you've got 10 minutes this week, I'd love to show you how it works. No pitch, just a live walkthrough.

Best, Patrik Matheson AOM | aheadofmarket.com

Email 2: Value-add (Day 4)

Subject: How Phoenix contractors are using AI

Hi [First Name],

Following up on my note earlier. I put together a market breakdown showing how contractors in the Phoenix area are starting to use AI for estimating, scheduling, and client communication.

[Link to market breakdown doc or blog post]

Quick read. If any of it resonates, happy to walk you through what we've built.

Best, Patrik

Email 3: Direct CTA (Day 9)

Subject: Last note

Hi [First Name],

Don't want to crowd your inbox. Last note from me.

We're onboarding our first 5 construction companies onto our AI operations platform this quarter. Each gets a dedicated AI team that handles scheduling, client follow-up, estimating support, and daily admin.

If the timing isn't right, no worries at all. But if you're curious, I'm at [phone] or just reply here.

Patrik

Sequence 2: CPA Firms (Cold)

Email 1: Open the door (Day 0)

Subject: Tax season + AI

Hi [First Name],

Quick question: how many hours does your team spend chasing clients for documents during tax season?

We built an AI system that handles document collection reminders, deadline tracking, and client communication for CPA firms. Automatically. Not a chatbot. A team of AI agents that knows your deadlines and follows up before you have to.

If you've got 10 minutes, I'd love to show you how it works. Live demo, not a slide deck.

Best, Patrik Matheson AOM | aheadofmarket.com

Email 2-3: Same pattern as construction (value-add doc, then direct CTA).

Objection Handling

"It's too expensive." "I hear you. Let me put it this way: $3k/month is about $140/business day. If Corner saves you 2 hours a day of admin work, and your time is worth $100/hour, that's $200/day in value. You're getting $200 for $140. The ROI calculator shows exactly what the math looks like for your business."

"I don't trust AI." "Smart to be cautious. Here's what's different: you see everything the AI does. Every task, every email draft, every decision. Nothing goes out without your approval until you're comfortable. And your data is completely isolated. No one else, not even us, can see your business information."

"We tried [ChatGPT / some other tool] and it didn't work." "ChatGPT is one tool doing one thing. Corner is a team. Multiple AI agents working together, handing things off, checking each other's work. That's the difference between typing a question into a box and having an operations team. Let me show you what I mean."

"We're too small for this." "Actually, you're exactly who this is for. Big companies hire 10 people for their back office. You can't afford that. Corner gives you that team for $3k/month. The smaller you are, the bigger the impact."

"What if the AI makes a mistake?" "It will. So do employees. The difference: Corner has a QA agent that reviews work before it reaches you. And when it does make a mistake, it learns. Over time, mistakes go down, not up. Plus, you have final approval on anything client-facing."

"I need to think about it." "Of course. Here's what I'd suggest: the audit. $2,500 flat. We spend two weeks understanding your operations. At the end, you get a report showing exactly where AI saves you time and money. If it doesn't convince you, you've still got a useful operational analysis. No ongoing commitment. Just the audit."

"Can I talk to one of your clients?" "Absolutely. We're running this for our own business. I'll give you a full walkthrough of our real system. And I can connect you with [Ambition Mechanical / other client] who's been using our services."

Pricing Presentation

How to talk about pricing (not a rate card, a conversation):

"Corner has four tiers. Most businesses start at Growth, which is $3,000 a month."

Pause. Let them process. Don't explain further until they respond.

If they seem fine: "That includes 6 AI agents, full skills access, and everything you need to run your operations. We handle all the setup."

If they react to the price: "Let me show you the math." Open ROI calculator. Input their numbers. Show the payback.

Comparison anchors (use whichever resonates):

  • "That's less than one part-time employee."
  • "That's what you'd pay a bookkeeper for 15 hours a month. Corner works 24/7."
  • "Your last hire probably cost you $5k/month fully loaded. And they called in sick."
  • "If Corner saves you 10 hours a week of admin, and your time is worth $100/hour, that's $4,000/month in value for $3,000."

Never discount. If they can't afford $3k/month, offer the audit ($2,500 one-time) instead. If they can't afford the audit, they're not the right client. Move on.

90-Day Launch Sprint

Days 1-30: Foundation

Week 1:

  • Patrik and Ash each list 20 warm contacts
  • Jacob segments AZ ROC database for Phoenix metro contractors
  • Alex drafts 3 LinkedIn posts about AI for small business
  • Download AZ ROC CSV (Patrik, 2 minutes)

Week 2:

  • Patrik sends personal messages to top 10 warm contacts
  • Jacob sends Email 1 to first 50 cold prospects
  • Alex publishes first LinkedIn post
  • Schedule 3-5 discovery calls from warm network

Week 3:

  • Conduct discovery calls
  • Jacob sends Email 2 to first 50, Email 1 to next 50
  • In-person demos for warm leads
  • Alex publishes second LinkedIn post

Week 4:

  • Close first audit ($2,500)
  • Jacob sends Email 3 to first 50, Email 2 to next 50, Email 1 to next 50
  • Follow up on all open demos
  • Publish blog post: "How We Built an AI Operations System for Our Business"

Days 31-60: Acceleration

  • Complete first audit, deliver report
  • Convert first audit to ongoing client ($3k/month)
  • Continue cold outreach (100 new prospects/week)
  • In-person demos for cold-sourced leads
  • Second LinkedIn post series
  • Second blog post
  • Ask first client for referral

Days 61-90: Scale

  • Target: 5 paying clients
  • Launch referral program
  • Refine email sequences based on response data
  • Start CPA outreach sequence (tax season messaging)
  • Produce client case study (video + written)
  • Third blog post series
  • Evaluate: what's working, what's not, adjust

Metrics to Track

Metric Target Frequency
Emails sent 100/week Weekly
Reply rate >5% Weekly
Discovery calls booked 5/week Weekly
Demos completed 3/week Weekly
Audits sold 2/month Monthly
Clients closed 2-3/month Monthly
MRR $15k by day 90 Monthly
Churn <5% monthly Monthly
NPS from existing clients 8+ Monthly

What Alex Owns

  • LinkedIn content strategy and drafts
  • Blog post outlines and first drafts
  • Competitive positioning if a prospect mentions alternatives
  • Refinement of the market breakdown doc (the value-add in Email 2)
  • Case study content from AOM's own usage

What Jacob Owns

  • AZ ROC database segmentation and maintenance
  • Cold email sending (sequences, tracking, optimization)
  • Reply routing to Patrik
  • Email deliverability monitoring
  • Multi-domain email infrastructure (pending purchase approval)

What Patrik Owns

  • Warm outreach (personal messages)
  • Discovery calls
  • In-person demos
  • Closing
  • Audit delivery
  • Client relationship (post-close)
  • Final approval on all outgoing communications

What Ash Owns

  • Operations once clients are onboarded
  • Invoice collection and payment tracking
  • Client escalations
  • Referral conversations with existing clients

The first client changes everything. Before the first client, Corner is a vision. After the first client, Corner is a business. Every spec, every design, every line of code exists to get to that moment. This playbook is how.
